title: Adapter paved road
design: The Nth source is a mapping exercise. The paved road is map, declare, resolve identity, build via the shared library, prove fail closed, register.
acceptance_criteria: Adding an adapter changes no existing adapter, consumer, or shared runtime. Adapter change ratio is zero.

title: Sessions and coverage
design: Coverage is derived from registered manifests. Sessions terminate on a rule: schedule, expiry, retention, or case closure. Explicit close is the exception.
acceptance_criteria: Coverage for a subject lists adapters, fidelity, and modes. A session outside its window is closed without an operator.

title: Subject identity
design: Raw identifiers resolve to a canonical subject with confidence. Ambiguity resolves to no subject. Correction is auditable and retroactive. Erasure spans estates.
acceptance_criteria: Conflicting claims produce unresolved + diagnostic, never a silent merge. SAR retrieve and erase work across managed and self-hosted estates subject to hold.

title: Collection authority
design: Deny by default. Mode determines the approver. Jurisdiction follows the subject. Every grant is bounded. Every denial is actionable.
acceptance_criteria: subject-0002 in DE is denied continuous_screen with a reason naming the jurisdiction; subject-0001 in US-NC is granted with expires_at.

title: Contracts and vocabulary
design: The five contracts plus taxonomy.yaml are the published language. Everything downstream is an implementation of them.
acceptance_criteria: make validate passes; every adapter manifest cross-checks the taxonomy; contract tests cover determinism, hash chaining, and fail closed.

title: Rule and threshold compatibility report
design: Before cutover, classify every tenant authored rule as identical, changed, or dependent on a retired signal type. This is what converts migration from a leap of faith into a reviewable decision.
acceptance_criteria: Report names each rule and its classification; a tenant with any changed rule cannot be cut over without explicit acknowledgement.

title: JDBC PolicyRepository implementation
design: Back the interface with the tables in tools/schema.sql. Tenant scoped queries only; a query without a tenant predicate must not compile.
acceptance_criteria: Integration test seeds both demo subjects and asserts grant and denial paths against a real database.

title: Control plane
design: Synchronous and low volume. Subject resolution, authority decisions, session lifecycle, adapter registry. Never on the telemetry path.
acceptance_criteria: Authority decisions are issued from persisted policy; a denial always carries a reason; no granted decision lacks an expiry.

title: Contracts and taxonomy
design: The four schemas plus taxonomy.yaml are the architecture. Everything downstream is an implementation of them, so this epic gates the rest.
acceptance_criteria: make validate passes; every adapter manifest cross checks against the taxonomy; contract tests cover determinism, hash chaining, and fail closed.

title: Migration programme
design: Assessment, compatibility, read-path first, collection switch, history, rollback, decommission. Tooling is the product. Cost per tenant and rollback rate are first-class metrics.
acceptance_criteria: A tenant is assessed, cut over, and rolled back without a bespoke runbook. Changed compatibility cannot cut over without recorded acknowledgement.
notes: later phase; not on the ready queue

title: Outbound estate shipper
design: Deployed in the customer estate. Outbound only. Checkpoint advances only after ack. Health is self-reported on the same channel.
acceptance_criteria: Restart resumes from checkpoint; replay is absorbed; skip is impossible. No listening port.
notes: later phase; not on the ready queue

title: Scoring and tenant rules
design: Derived values carry model_version. Version is pinned per tenant. Platform migration never coincides with a model change. Rules cannot be authored unbounded or against missing vocab.
acceptance_criteria: A tenant with model 1.4.0 never sees 1.5.0 scores until a separate upgrade with a comparison period.
notes: later phase; not on the ready queue

title: Federated read
design: One read interface across estates. Fan-out with a deadline. Merge on signal_id. Partial results named. Reads themselves are audited.
acceptance_criteria: With one estate down, results return, labelled partial, naming the estate. Duplicates collapse. Read audit records who/what/when/case.
notes: later phase; not on the ready queue

title: Persistence
design: Index for retrieval by subject and time, tenant-first partitioned. Object store for bytes with retention lock and hold. Residency is topology. Keys may be customer held.
acceptance_criteria: Cross-tenant read is inexpressible. Hold refuses deletion at the store. Dangling reference count is zero.
notes: later phase; not on the ready queue

title: Transport and quality
design: Records on an event stream partitioned so subject order is preserved. Invalid records divert, never silently drop or accept.
acceptance_criteria: Topic per category; partition key tenant|subject; diverted volume by adapter is a monitored quality signal.
notes: later phase; not on the ready queue

title: Source adapters
design: One adapter per source, independently deployed. The estate is a source, not a peer. directory_watch is the reference shape.
acceptance_criteria: Two adapters run concurrently without cross interference. Estate ingest is just another adapter.
notes: later phase; not on the ready queue

title: Estate migration tooling
design: The measure is cost per tenant migrated and rollback rate. If a migration needs an engineer on a call it reaches only the loudest customers. The tooling is the product.
acceptance_criteria: A tenant can be assessed, cut over, and rolled back without a bespoke runbook.

title: Read path
design: Federated read across estates, merged on signal_id, partial results reported.
acceptance_criteria: A failing estate degrades the response honestly instead of hiding data.

title: Ingest path
design: One adapter per source, emitting to the bus, blobs by reference.
acceptance_criteria: Two adapters run concurrently without one degrading the other.

title: Integrator can exercise an adapter with no infrastructure

title: Reliability engineer is told when a source goes silent
design: NFR observability. Silent failures rate above loud ones.
acceptance_criteria: No events from directory_watch for 3× min_interval pages an owner.

title: Absence detection
design: A source that stops emitting looks like a subject who did nothing. AR-11.
acceptance_criteria: Alert when volume is below the declared minimum interval multiple.

title: Redrive API scoped to one adapter
Operator redrives records that could not be processed
design: FR-2.5. Diverted volume is a quality signal.
acceptance_criteria: DLQ for adapter A is isolated; redrive republishes valid records only.

title: Isolation and failure channel
design: Saturation in one adapter must not move another adapter's error rate. Each has a DLQ and redrive.
acceptance_criteria: Load on adapter A does not raise errors on adapter B. Redrive is operator initiated.

title: A saturated source does not degrade any other source
acceptance_criteria: Chaos test: throttle A, B's error rate and latency stay within baseline.

title: add-adapter formula covers the paved sequence
Worked example for a second source
Integrator adds a source without a bespoke checklist
design: §13.3. Conformant path is the fastest path.
acceptance_criteria: bd mol pour add-adapter --var adapter_id=... creates the task graph.

title: Paved-road formula
design: add-adapter formula: map vocabulary, declare capability, identity, implement, fail-closed test, register, review.
acceptance_criteria: Pouring add-adapter for a named source produces the molecule; departing from it requires ARB.

title: CI grep for hand-rolled schema_version keys
Integrator cannot ship an adapter that bypasses authority
design: AR-01. No override path.
acceptance_criteria: Grep/CI fails if an adapter imports json and writes an envelope by hand.

title: Shared library is the only emit path
design: Record construction, identity, integrity, authority live here. Adapter N+1 cannot drift.
acceptance_criteria: No public constructor for envelopes outside AdapterContext.build.

title: Case closure terminates every session on that case
design: UC4 case closure rule.
acceptance_criteria: Closing a case closes child sessions within the terminator interval.

title: Administrator can explicitly close a session
design: Exception path, auditable.
acceptance_criteria: POST close records actor and reason; subsequent emit is refused.

title: Terminator loop on schedule and expiry
Session record with window and decision_id
Collection stops at the schedule window without an operator
acceptance_criteria: Clock past window.end closes the session and adapters fail closed.

title: Rule-driven session lifecycle
design: UC4. Sessions die on schedule boundary, decision expiry, retention clock, or case closure.
acceptance_criteria: A session past expiry is closed; explicit termination exists and is logged as exceptional.

title: Ambiguous identifier does not guess coverage
Administrator sees which sources can observe a subject before opening a session
design: UC2.
acceptance_criteria: GET /v1/subjects/{id}/coverage names adapters, fidelity, and modes; ambiguity returns 409 with diagnostic.

title: Coverage discovery
design: Which sources can observe this subject, at what fidelity, under which modes — from manifests, not tribal knowledge.
acceptance_criteria: Given an identifier, coverage lists adapters whose identifier_kinds and capture_modes apply.

title: Integrator registers a manifest and it becomes visible to coverage
acceptance_criteria: POST /v1/adapters then GET coverage includes the new adapter.

title: Adapter registry
design: Registration is how coverage becomes a derived answer.
acceptance_criteria: Registered manifests are queryable by adapter_id and version; seed.py is idempotent.

title: Erase across index, blobs, and identifier maps
Subject erasure is refused while a legal hold applies
design: Hold is storage-layer enforcement.
acceptance_criteria: DELETE subject is 409 while hold is on; after hold release, index and blobs are gone.

title: Include authority provenance in the export
Subject receives everything the platform holds about them
acceptance_criteria: Export job returns index rows and payload refs for one subject_id from every estate.

title: SAR export job across federated read
Subject access and erasure
design: Retrievable and deletable by canonical subject across sources and estates, hold taking precedence.
acceptance_criteria: SAR export contains all estates; erase is refused while held and completes when hold lifts.

title: Correction ledger with actor and reason
Administrator splits a wrong merge and history follows
acceptance_criteria: After correction, records previously under subject A for identifier X appear under subject B.

title: Auditable correction
design: Mappings are correctable. Correction reapplies across stored records.
acceptance_criteria: An administrator can split a merged identity; subsequent reads use the corrected subject.

title: Diagnostic on unresolved, no subject_id issued
Ambiguous claims do not invent a person
design: FR-3.2, AR-08. Silent merge is the identity failure that matters.
acceptance_criteria: Email mapped to two subject_ids returns unresolved and a diagnostic event.

title: Investigator's query by email finds the same subject as a query by device id
acceptance_criteria: Two identifier kinds for subject-0001 resolve to the same subject_id.

title: Identifier to canonical subject
design: UPN, email, device id, account SID, employee number are claims, not the subject.
acceptance_criteria: A known mapping returns subject_id and confidence; unknown returns unresolved, not a new person guessed from email.

title: Decision audit trail
design: Every decision, granted or denied, is persisted with its inputs.
acceptance_criteria: A decision_id resolves to policy version, approver, inputs, and outcome.

title: Compliance owner traces a stored record to the decision that permitted it
acceptance_criteria: GET /v1/authority/decisions/{id} returns the full decision including inputs.

title: Document revocation latency as the decision lifetime
Works council withdraws approval and capture stops before the next TTL
design: FR-4.10. Adapters do not refresh a revoked decision.
acceptance_criteria: After approval row is deleted, a new evaluate returns denied; in-flight session dies at expiry.

title: Delete approval invalidates new evaluates immediately
Revocation within the decision lifetime
design: Withdrawal takes effect within the cached TTL. Shortening TTL increases control-plane load. This is a designed bound.
acceptance_criteria: Revoking approval stops capture within max_lifetime_seconds.

title: Adapter filters excluded destinations before build
Banking and health destinations are never captured regardless of tenant config
design: FR-4.12. Jurisdictional never-collect list.
acceptance_criteria: Payload or metadata destined to *.bank.example is dropped even with a grant.

title: Adapter refuses emit outside the window
Stamp schedule_windows from policy onto the decision
Collection is closed outside the permitted schedule window
design: FR-4.7, UC4. Session termination is rule driven.
acceptance_criteria: A decision with weekday windows refuses emit on Sunday.

title: Decision constraints
design: Schedule windows, excluded categories, excluded destinations, redaction profile travel with the grant.
acceptance_criteria: A grant outside a window is unusable; excluded destinations are never captured.

title: Adapter raises AuthorityDenied and does not retry
Caller does not retry a denial as if it were a 5xx
design: A denial is a well-formed answer.
acceptance_criteria: POST /v1/authority/decisions returns 200 and granted=false.

title: Denial for no approval on record
Denial for no policy on file
Administrator can act on a denial without reading source code
design: FR-4.6. Reasons name missing approval, missing jurisdiction, or mode not permitted.
acceptance_criteria: Each deny branch in AuthorityGate has a distinct reason string covering the cause.

title: Actionable denial
design: A denial nobody can explain is indistinguishable from a bug and gets worked around.
acceptance_criteria: Every denial has denial_reason an administrator can act on; HTTP 200 with granted=false.

title: Adapter stops emitting when the cached grant expires
design: NFR-1.1 converse: in-flight collection continues only while the decision is unexpired.
acceptance_criteria: After expiry, the next build() raises and no envelope is produced.

title: Reject granted && expires_at == null in AuthorityDecision constructor
Administrator receives a time-bounded grant for a permitted mode
design: FR-4.5. US-NC subject-0001 passive_metadata with employer approval.
acceptance_criteria: granted=true and expires_at = evaluated_at + max_lifetime_seconds.

title: Bounded grant
design: Every granted decision has expires_at. max_lifetime_seconds on the policy is the bound.
acceptance_criteria: No granted decision lacks expiry. Cache lifetime cannot exceed the decision.

title: Test: employer approval does not satisfy DE override
Works-council override replaces the mode default approver
design: DE permitted_modes is passive_metadata only; approver_override is works_council.
acceptance_criteria: Approval from employer is ignored when override is works_council.

title: Denial reason includes jurisdiction and mode
Investigator in DE is not captured at continuous_screen without works-council approval
design: UC3. Governing rule follows the subject.
acceptance_criteria: evaluate(tenant-demo, subject-0002, continuous_screen) returns granted=false and names DE.

title: Capture mode and subject jurisdiction
design: Approver is a function of mode and optional jurisdiction override. Tenant HQ is irrelevant.
acceptance_criteria: DE subject cannot use a US-NC employer grant; works_council override is honoured.

title: Changing policy does not alter previously issued decision rows
Stamp policy_version from the row used
Policy version on the decision is the version that was applied
design: FR-4.2, NFR-4.4. Retroactive policy change does not rewrite history.
acceptance_criteria: Granted decision.policy_version equals jurisdiction_policy.policy_version at evaluation time.

title: Integration test against local Postgres seed
Tenant predicate required on every query
Administrator's grant is evaluated against stored policy, not a stub
design: UC3 / FR-4.1. E2.F1.T2 of the old plan: JDBC PolicyRepository.
acceptance_criteria: AuthorityGate.evaluate reads jurisdiction_policy, subject, and approval tables.

title: Persisted jurisdictional policy
design: Policy lives in the store, not in code. JDBC repository is tenant-scoped; a query without tenant does not compile.
acceptance_criteria: Integration test seeds both demo subjects and asserts grant and denial against a real database.

title: CI check that generated output is not stale
Codegen from JSON Schema into Portals/shared
Portal compile fails when the envelope schema changes incompatibly
design: Shared library owns generation. Hand-written TS models are prohibited.
acceptance_criteria: Changing a required envelope field breaks portal CI.

title: Generated contract models for portals
design: Types are generated from Contracts/schemas so a contract change is a compile error, not a runtime surprise.
acceptance_criteria: Fresh clone of admin-portal and client-portal builds without a codegen step; generated output is committed.

title: Registry rejects a manifest with empty identifier_kinds
Identifier kinds on the manifest drive subject resolution
design: The control plane must not guess which identifiers an adapter will send.
acceptance_criteria: Coverage for a subject includes only adapters whose identifier kinds can bind.

title: Integrator declares capability before shipping
design: FR-2.2. Coverage discovery reads this, not tribal knowledge.
acceptance_criteria: A manifest missing capture_modes or emits fails validate.

title: Adapter manifest contract
design: Coverage is derived from manifests. An inaccurate manifest produces confidently wrong coverage.
acceptance_criteria: Manifest schema requires emits, capture_modes, delivery, identifier kinds; CI validates it.

title: Adapter blob helper writes then returns the reference
Test: no payload_ref if write fails
A reference to absent content cannot be published
design: Orphans are recoverable; dangling refs are not.
acceptance_criteria: Shared library refuses to attach payload_ref before the write ack.

title: Envelope payload_ref uses the blob schema
Blob reference schema fields: uri, hash, media_type, bytes, retention, hold, key, estate
Payload reference contract
design: Bulk never rides the bus. Write bytes first, publish the reference second.
acceptance_criteria: blob-reference.schema.json is complete; envelope payload_ref $ref resolves.

title: A record carries a reference, never the bytes
design: FR-5.2. Retention has one enforcement point.
acceptance_criteria: Envelope with inline bytes fails schema validation.

title: Align SQL seed approver with schema
Persisted approver roles match the contract enums
design: Approver mapping is the gate. Case mismatch is a silent deny-all or deny-none.
acceptance_criteria: Seed approvals use subject, employer, works_council.

title: Persisted capture modes match the contract enums
design: Uppercase seed values would fail runtime validation and block the gate.
acceptance_criteria: Seed data and schema both use passive_metadata and friends.

title: Align SQL seed capture_mode with schema
Control plane deny path always stamps expires_at
Authority decision contract
design: Bounded permission. Capture mode names the approver. Jurisdiction follows the subject. Unbounded grants are invalid.
acceptance_criteria: Schema requires expires_at; capture_mode and approver.role enums match persisted policy values.

title: A decision without expiry cannot be issued
design: ADR-0004. expires_at is required, including on denials, so caches always have a bound.
acceptance_criteria: JSON Schema validation fails when expires_at is absent.

title: Removing a signal type requires a new schema_version and an ADR
design: FR-1.3. Repurposing a key is a breaking change.
acceptance_criteria: docs/ describes the bump procedure with a worked example.

title: Contract test that unclassified emit is impossible
Unmapped event path in shared library
Integrator cannot emit an unclassified record
design: FR-1.8. Gap is declared; the event is diverted or rejected, never stored as other.
acceptance_criteria: Handler that cannot map an event records a declared gap and does not call build().

title: Fail validation when PyYAML is absent rather than skipping
Release is blocked when an adapter invents a signal type
design: Vocabulary governance is mechanical. AR-04 / R1.
acceptance_criteria: validate.py exits non-zero on an unknown signal_type.

title: Governed vocabulary
design: Additive only within a schema_version. An unmapped event is a decision, not an unclassified record.
acceptance_criteria: A manifest with an unknown signal_type or invalid category fails CI; a taxonomy addition alone does not.

title: Treat missing expires_at as expired in is_expired
Capture is refused without an unexpired authority decision
design: Fail closed. Missing or expired authority is a defect, not a configuration choice.
acceptance_criteria: build() raises PermissionError when authority is absent or expired.

title: Contract test for chain linkage and per-subject isolation
Per subject hash chain in AdapterContext
Investigator can detect omitted records without trusting the store
design: Per-subject content hash chain. Integrity is evidential, not decorative.
acceptance_criteria: Consecutive signals for one subject link; a second subject starts a new chain.

title: Deterministic v5 signal_id over tenant, adapter, native id
Replay of the same source event collapses to one record
design: signal_id is uuid5 of tenant|adapter|native_id so overlap during migration does not double count.
acceptance_criteria: Two builds with the same native_id produce the same signal_id.

title: Reject additional properties and unknown signal types at validation
Integrator emits only the normalized envelope
design: Heterogeneity stops at the adapter. Consumers never see a source-specific shape.
acceptance_criteria: A directory_watch event validates against signal-envelope.schema.json with no additional properties.

title: Normalized envelope and shared construction library
design: Adapters build records only through AdapterContext so identity, hashing, and authority checks cannot drift.
acceptance_criteria: No adapter can emit a record without an unexpired decision; signal_id is deterministic; hash chain is per subject.

title: Smoke test covering the known divergences
Cost guardrail alarm on the dev stage
Cloud smoke path
design: Local green does not guarantee cloud green. The divergences that bite are IAM, MSK auth, partition behaviour, object lock, and cold starts.
acceptance_criteria: The smoke path exercises all five and runs before any release.

title: OIDC deploy role and least privilege policy
Stack verification
design: Core, Ingest, and ControlPlane deploy and destroy independently.
acceptance_criteria: Destroying ControlPlane loses no data; Ingest redeploys without touching Core.

title: First deploy of the dev stage
Cloud deployment
design: Small separable stacks, manual dispatch only, destroy as a first class operation.
acceptance_criteria: A stage can be brought up, smoke tested, and destroyed from the workflow alone.

title: Scoped views
design: Group and user filters are convenience; scope is enforced server side.
acceptance_criteria: The UI never offers a scope the caller does not hold.

title: Qualify counts when results are partial
Honest partial results
design: Render a banner naming the unavailable estate. A console that silently returns half the data during an investigation is worse than one that errors.
acceptance_criteria: With one estate down, the UI names it and the result count is qualified.

title: Console scaffold
design: Angular with a dev proxy to the broker and control plane.
acceptance_criteria: ng serve reaches both services without CORS workarounds.

title: Console
design: One UI across both estates during migration.
acceptance_criteria: Partial results are visible; scope is never merely cosmetic.

title: Cost per tenant and rollback rate metrics
Cutover and rollback
design: Each of the four migration steps is independently reversible.
acceptance_criteria: A cutover can be reversed within the rollback window with no data loss.

title: Legal hold carries across the boundary
Backfill versus age out cost model
Backfill and retention decision
design: Index and metadata migrate first; bytes may age out under retention instead of moving. For most tenants the retention window is shorter than the migration programme.
acceptance_criteria: Per tenant, the tool recommends backfill or age out with the cost of each.

title: Threshold drift estimate under the pinned model
Static analysis of tenant rules against the taxonomy
Self reported health over the outbound channel
Edge shipper
design: Outbound only, durable checkpoint written atomically after acknowledgement.
acceptance_criteria: A restart resumes from the checkpoint; replay is absorbed, skipping is not possible.

title: Signed handle broker for estate resident blobs
Blob resolution across estates
design: Bytes may remain in a self hosted estate during migration. The broker mints short lived references rather than proxying the bytes.
acceptance_criteria: A reference resolvable_from self_hosted returns a time bounded handle.

title: Signal index writer from the bus
Index backed estate
design: Replace StubEstate with an implementation over the signal index, partitioned by tenant and subject so a cross tenant read cannot be expressed.
acceptance_criteria: A query without tenant scope fails at the type level, not at runtime. Broker tests pass unchanged against the real implementation.

title: Query broker federation
design: Concurrent fan out with a deadline; merge on signal_id; managed plane wins ties.
acceptance_criteria: Duplicate merge and partial result behaviour are covered by tests.

title: Failure isolation
design: Per adapter DLQ routing and per source concurrency limits.
acceptance_criteria: A saturated adapter does not raise error rates on any other adapter.

title: Bearer authentication and per tenant rate limit
Estate ingest endpoint
design: Receives batches from the edge shipper. Idempotent by signal_id, so a replayed batch after a checkpoint failure is absorbed rather than doubled.
acceptance_criteria: Submitting the same batch twice produces the same stored state.

title: Blob write ordering
design: Blob durable first, reference published second. Orphaned blobs are swept; dangling references are not acceptable.
acceptance_criteria: A fault injected between write and publish leaves an orphan, never a dangling reference. The sweeper reclaims it.

title: Reference adapter and emission
design: Directory watch adapter demonstrating the full shape end to end.
acceptance_criteria: Runs with or without a broker present; output validates against the schema.

title: Session lifecycle and coverage discovery
design: Coverage discovery answers which adapters can observe a subject, from the registered manifests. Sessions terminate on a rule: schedule boundary, decision expiry, retention clock, or case closure.
acceptance_criteria: A session outside its schedule window is closed automatically; explicit termination is available but is not the normal path.

title: Identifier to subject mapping and confidence
Subject resolution
design: Map raw identifiers (upn, email, device id, account sid) to one canonical subject with a confidence score. Ambiguity resolves to no subject rather than a guess.
acceptance_criteria: Conflicting identifier claims produce an unresolved result and a diagnostic, never a silent merge of two people.

title: Authority decision audit trail
design: Every decision, granted or denied, is persisted with its inputs.
acceptance_criteria: A decision id can be resolved to the policy version and approval that produced it.

title: Decision cache invalidation on policy change
design: Adapters hold decisions for their bounded lifetime. A revocation must take effect within the decision lifetime, which bounds exposure.
acceptance_criteria: Revoking approval stops capture within the configured lifetime.

title: Authority gate
design: Deny by default. Jurisdiction follows the subject, not the tenant. Approver role is derived from capture mode and may be overridden per jurisdiction.
acceptance_criteria: subject-0002 in DE is denied CONTINUOUS_SCREEN with a reason naming the jurisdiction; subject-0001 in US-NC is granted with a bounded expiry.

title: Schema version bump procedure
design: Document what forces a new schema_version and how adapters migrate.
acceptance_criteria: docs/ describes the procedure; a worked example exists.

title: Fail validation when PyYAML is absent rather than skipping
design: validate.py currently prints a notice and passes when PyYAML is missing, so the taxonomy check can silently not run.
acceptance_criteria: Missing PyYAML causes a non zero exit with a clear message.

title: Taxonomy governance
design: Additive only within a schema_version. The validator fails any manifest emitting a signal_type the taxonomy does not know.
acceptance_criteria: A manifest with an unknown signal type or invalid category fails CI; a taxonomy addition alone does not.

title: Envelope schema and shared adapter library
design: Deterministic v5 signal_id over tenant, adapter, native id. Per subject hash chain. Envelope construction lives in the shared library so adapters cannot drift.
acceptance_criteria: Contract tests prove id determinism, chain linkage, per subject chain isolation, and refusal both without authority and after expiry.

title: Scoring model version pinned per tenant

Control plane stays off the telemetry hot path
